rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CIV prorogator Life Hylech Hyleg Apheta
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A separate chapter introduces Hylech/Hyleg/Apheta as the alleged prorogator of life and an interficient/killing planet.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Printed CIV/editorial CV, separate from infant-survival chapter above page561 divider.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: word Chaldean planet or place heaven
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly describes Hylech as a Chaldean term for a planet or place of Heaven.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Period astrological terminology, not medical prognostic variable.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: which being directed judge Life estate thereof
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A selected planet or point's direction is claimed to determine life or its state.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No verified individual time-of-death or survival outcome.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Hylech thus found in Diurnall take Sun, Nocturnall Moon
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The first branch starts with Sun for daytime and Moon for nighttime births.
rules.original_source_qualifications: The rule crosses PDF561–562; one conditional branch, not two unrelated predictions.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: convenient Hylegiacall places houses first tenth eleventh seventh ninth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Sun or Moon can be accepted as Hyleg only in the first, tenth, eleventh, seventh or ninth houses or their stated orbs.
rules.original_source_qualifications: House-set admissibility is source critical.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: within Orbs houses
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The eligiblity extends to planets within house orbs.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Exact numerical house orb not supplied here.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: space Equator under earth rejected
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Sun/Moon below the horizon are rejected as candidate Hyleg under the general rule.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source gives an explicit Ascendant-near exception.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: unless within twenty five degrees ascendant
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A planet below Earth within 25 degrees of Ascendant is an exception.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Specific 25-degree angular threshold must be preserved.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: eighth house and twelfth rejected
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Sun or Moon positioned in eighth or twelfth house is rejected as a Hyleg candidate.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Another hard source prohibition.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if Sun not capable then Moon
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: In the default preference order, if Sun's position disqualifies it Lilly checks the Moon.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Preserve ordered fallback rather than selecting Moon freely.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if neither consider if geniture diurnall new Moon precede
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: If neither luminary qualifies and birth is diurnal, inspect preceding new Moon.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source branch refers to event before birth.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: nocturnal observe full Moon going before Birth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: In night births the preceding full Moon is considered.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Separate from diurnal new-Moon branch.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Planet hath most dominion these places
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He asks which planet rules the chosen syzygy degree via essential dignities.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Requires historical dignity scores and epoch data.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: least three essential fortitudes
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The dignity candidate must possess at least three essential fortitudes at selected place.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source threshold; not independent outcome correlation.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Planet in Hylegiacall house
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The selected dignity-holder must also lie in an eligible Hylegical house.
rules.original_source_qualifications: An essential conjunct condition, not optional.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if not apt house simply let Horoscope be Hyleg
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: If strongest dignity-holder is not in an eligible house, use the Ascendant as Hyleg.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Ordered fallback, do not discard.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: some Artists ever use Ascendant
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly acknowledges that some astrologers always take Ascendant as Hyleg and reject other methods.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Competing historical choice, not corroborating result.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: diurnall ever regard degree New Moon preceding though full intervened
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: For a day birth he says to consider the earlier new-Moon degree even if a full Moon intervened shortly before birth.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Could conflict with simpler last-syzygy reading; preserve exact qualification.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: by day Sun more powerful than Moon
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He explains this diurnal preference through Sun's claimed greater power.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Not scientifically demonstrated.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: nocturnal consider Moon at Birth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: In a night chart one candidate position is Moon's degree at birth.
rules.original_source_qualifications: First of three night candidate positions.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: nocturnal place Opposition or full Moon preceding
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Night-chart candidates include preceding full-Moon/opposition degree.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Second candidate; historical syzygy calculation unverified.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: nocturnal Part of Fortune at Birth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The natal Part of Fortune is another candidate at night.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Third candidate; derived figure dependent on sect and chart calculations.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if such a Planet in Aphetical place he shall be Prorogator
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The strongest candidate planet is appointed the life prorogator if it occupies an eligible Aphetical position.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Candidate conditions inherited from previous page.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if not so new Moon preceded take Ascendant
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: If the dignity planet is not suitably placed and a new Moon preceded, Lilly takes the Ascendant.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Fallback branch.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if full Moon ... take Part Fortune if Aphetical else Ascendant
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: After a preceding full Moon, use Part of Fortune if eligible, otherwise Ascendant.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source distinctly uses Part of Fortune versus Ascendant.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: in nocturnal Births care to full Moon though conjunction next
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: In night births he says the preceding full Moon may still matter even if a new Moon follows near the birth.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source allows looking past the immediately preceding phase.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Luminary place degree where Light above earth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The source defines relevant luminary position in terms of the light being above the horizon at the syzygy.
rules.original_source_qualifications: May require specialized historic day/night syzygy context.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: both Lights ... Planet Governor proper place all Aphetical
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He also considers a case where both luminaries and a ruling planet occupy eligible life-significator places.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Multi-candidate comparison.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: place Light preferred greater virtue more apt place
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Choose the light judged stronger in dignities and more suitable house placement.
rules.original_source_qualifications: No fixed universally applied numerical score specified here.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: nocturnal Moon ninth or seventh Sun Ascendant prefer Sun
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: In a night chart, Sun in Ascendant may be preferred over Moon in ninth/seventh.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Example overrides naive automatic sect-first selection.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Sun nearer ascending or dignified within25 degrees
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: That preference strengthens if Sun is close to rising degree, essentially dignified or within 25° of Ascendant.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source explicit conditional.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: diurnal Moon tenth Sun ninth prefer Moon
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: In a day chart Moon in tenth may outrank Sun in ninth.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Another counterexample to always choosing the sect luminary.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon tenth Sun eleventh seem equal
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Moon in tenth and Sun in eleventh are described as roughly equal eligibility.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Requires tie resolution.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: break tie most essential or accidental dignities
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: To resolve comparable lights select one with greatest essential or accidental dignities.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Different from first fallback.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if equal see disposer applying good aspect
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: If still tied, examine whether a dispositor applies to either luminary favorably.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Adds further choice.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: potent dispositor favourable aspect strengthens Hyleg
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A strong dispositor aspecting candidate Hyleg favorably is said to make the life significator stronger.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Astrological assertion, not empirical survival proof.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: I rest not satisfied how take Hyleg aright
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly expressly says he remains unsatisfied about the correct way of selecting a Hyleg.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Major uncertainty: do not present procedure as reliably solved by its author.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: whom properly Killing Interficient Destroying Planet Anareta
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He also says he is uncertain which planet should properly count as the killing/Anareta planet.
rules.original_source_qualifications: The source admits definitional and selection ambiguity.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Ancients Anareta in eighth house
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He reports an ancient proposal that the Anareta be found in eighth house.
rules.original_source_qualifications: A theory from earlier practitioners, not his experimentally validated result.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: five degrees before cusp eighth or twenty five after
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The cited Anareta definition extends from five degrees before the eighth cusp to twenty-five degrees afterward.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Specific 5°/25° window; verify use of cusp direction and orientation.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: five degrees before eighth cusp or twenty five after
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The eighth-house Anareta boundary continues from the preceding page.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Completes one earlier 5°/25° source window, not a new alternative definition.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Secondly Lord of eighth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The eighth-house ruler is a second candidate for the interficient planet.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Different from a planet physically in eighth.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Thirdly planet joyned to Lord eighth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A planet conjunct the eighth ruler is cited as a third candidate.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Lilly explicitly disapproves of this branch.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: which I no wayes approve of
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He states he does not approve the conjunction-to-eighth-lord candidate.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Must preserve negative disposition, not list all candidates as endorsed.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Fourthly Dispositor Lord eighth or planet in eighth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A planet dispositor of eighth ruler, or dispositor of a planet in eighth, is a fourth candidate.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Depends on ruler/occupancy selection.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Montulmo will not have sextile Saturn Mars kill
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The marginal note reports a disagreement by Montulmo about alleged destructive sextiles.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Competing earlier author opinion, not an observed death outcome.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: dexter sextile Saturn sinister dexter Mars long ascensions
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly describes traditional assignments treating certain sextiles of Saturn/Mars in long-ascension signs as dangerous.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Only in stated contexts, not all sextiles.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: sickly genitures climacterical yeeres other directions
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The sextile allegations are especially associated with already ill or climacteric-age charts and concurrent malefic directions.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Combines prior health with chart: selection bias and circular prediction risk.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Terms of Infortunes if not propitious
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He records another rule treating terms of malefics as dangerous when infortunes are not propitious.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source-specific term dignities and conditioning.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Arabians directions to cusps sixth eighth seventh fourth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He attributes fatal directional significators to Arabic astrology for sixth, eighth, seventh and sometimes fourth-house cusp.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Distinct historical source tradition.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: fourth cusp if watery Sign
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The fourth-cusp direction condition depends on the cusp being in a water sign.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Specific sign-sector conditional.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Dark Cloudy Nebulous parts Ecliptick
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Dark or cloudy ecliptic regions are listed as dangerous directional points.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Historical symbolic zones not independently defined here.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Eclipse Comet Azimene degrees
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Eclipses, comets and azimene degrees are added as alleged adverse locations.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Extensive candidate set with unverified astronomical/prognostic causality.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: square or opposition Mercury
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A square or opposition of Mercury is also listed in these claimed fatal directions.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source specifies certain angular aspects; cannot substitute others.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Moon or Mars obviate Ascendant rule eighth
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He reports Moon/Mars contacts toward Ascendant as adverse where eighth-house dominion applies.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Conjunction of contact and rulership.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Alcochodon giver of years
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He introduces Alcochodon as a historical 'giver of years' chosen near the Hyleg.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Not an observed numerical life expectancy predictor.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Planet most essential dignity in Hyleg place and aspects it
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The planet having most essential dignity at the Hyleg degree and beholding it by some aspect is proposed as Alcochodon.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Requires period essential dignity and aspect calculation.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: great greater lesser years planet signifies
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: It supposedly grants a planet-specific number of large/intermediate/small years.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Numeric years referenced elsewhere in book; not validated human survival outcomes.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: unless obstructive Directions hidden casualties general calamity
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He qualifies the year allotment by negative directions, sudden accidents and public calamities.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Ad hoc exception space makes fit less testable.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: no particular fate withstand general calamity
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He offers a general calamity exception to individual longevity expectations.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Contested metaphysical claim and retrospective exception.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: years every Planet from pages 57 to83 first part
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He points readers to earlier book pages for each planet's theoretical lifespan years.
rules.original_source_qualifications: The cross-referenced original numeric record needs independent table reading.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Luminary Hyleg in exaltation or house same Alcochodon
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: If Sun or Moon is Hyleg and in its own domicile or exaltation, it may serve as both Hyleg and Alcochodon.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Historical dual-role exception; begins PDF564.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if Hyleg luminary not house exaltation proper Terms sign ruler
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: If a luminary Hyleg is not in its own house, exaltation or terms, Lilly proposes the ruler of its sign as Alcochodon.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source sentence crosses original PDF564→565; one continuous branch.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: many Planets equal testimonies prefer aspect Hyleg
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: For competing equally dignified candidates, favor the one aspecting the Hyleg.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Conditional tie rule.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: if none aspect Hyleg prefer essential fortitudes
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: If no candidate aspects Hyleg, prefer greatest essential fortitudes.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Secondary branch after aspect tie.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: daytime Oriental before Occidental
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: For daytime charts he prefers a planet oriental rather than occidental.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Source-specific orientation criterion.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: angular strong first or tenth greater years
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: An Alcochodon in a strong angular house, especially first or tenth, is said to grant greater years.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Numerical 'greater years' not independently tested.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: not sufficiently satisfied either Hyleg Anareta Alcochodon
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: Lilly expressly states he is not satisfied with how these three categories are identified.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Crucial authorial reservation; procedure is not presented as certain by Lilly.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: intend see if own experience give more assured content
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He proposes seeking greater confidence through his own further observations.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Future work stated, not proof it later occurred.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: examination of many Nativities I have seen verified parties now all dead
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He says he has observed charts of people who are now dead and hopes to revisit them.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Historical retrospective sample not published with independent death data here.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: hope satisfy curiosity publish observations
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: He hopes to publish further observations and research on these methods.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Future intent only; do not invent a subsequent verified publication.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CV Of Lord of Geniture
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: A separate printed Chapter CV begins beneath the horizontal divider on PDF565.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Editorial sequential CVI, distinct from Hyleg life/death procedure.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: Ancients reject Firmicus Lord of Geniture
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The following chapter opens with disagreement about Firmicus's approach to the lord of the nativity.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Different subject, not Hyleg evidence.

rules.short_original_anchor_not_diplomatic: new chapter considers most essential dignities Asc MC Sun Moon Part Fortune
rules.historical_author_paraphrase: The following text considers planets with dignity in five principal natal places.
rules.original_source_qualifications: Belongs to printed CV and continues on PDF566, not accepted as Hyleg rules.
